title: The roofline
prompt: A kernel can't go faster than the machine's peak compute, and it can't go faster than memory can feed it. Write attainable(peak, bandwidth, flops, nbytes): the best speed in GFLOP/s a kernel doing flops operations on nbytes bytes of memory traffic can reach, on a machine with peak GFLOP/s and bandwidth GB/s.
hints: Arithmetic intensity is flops / nbytes: how many operations each byte you move pays for.
Memory can deliver bandwidth GB per second, so it can feed at most bandwidth · intensity GFLOP/s.
Take the smaller of that and peak.
explain: This is the roofline model. For low intensity (an elementwise add does about 1 operation per 12 bytes) memory is the limit, and a faster processor doesn't help. For high intensity (a big matmul reuses every number many times) compute is the limit. The first sample does 2 operations per byte: 20 GB/s times 2 is 40 GFLOP/s, under the 100 peak, so memory wins.
